articles.title: ‘I was too scared to stop’: Gurgaon biker recounts chase and crash on GCR
articles.summary: Gurgaon road rage: Woman biker Shivani Chauhan says a Maruti Ciaz chased and hit her on Golf Course Road. Accused arrested; police add attempt to murder, stalking charges.
articles.body: GURGAON: “I was very scared, so I did not stop.”Two days after a Maruti Ciaz chased and hit her on Golf Course Road, throwing her off her Aprilia and into the path of speeding traffic, Shivani Chauhan told TOI she never wanted a confrontation — she only wanted to get away.Shivani (27) said the ordeal began when the car came dangerously close to her motorcycle. The car first swept past her at high speed. “I thought, maybe, he had not seen me or was in a hurry. But if you have gone that fast, then go straight ahead. What sense does it make to stop ahead, gesture at me, then hit me from behind and run away?” she asked.Shivani said the car’s occupants repeatedly asked her to stop. “There were four boys in the vehicle. They were, perhaps, drunk and kept chasing me. They wanted to say something, but I did not want to talk,” she added.Shivani said she slowed to around 50-60kmph as the car moved across her path. She estimated it was travelling at around 100kmph or more when it came alongside and struck her. She was flung onto the road as her motorcycle skidded away, sparks flying from the friction.She suffered bruises and injuries to her knee and hand, but said the protective gear prevented fractures or worse. “I thank God that I had my riding shoes and gloves. The way my hand hit the road made me realise what could have happened. I could have broken my shoulder or legs.”The incident was captured on the camera mounted on her bike. Another camera also recorded the car moving across lanes before the collision.But one question still haunts her. What if the timing had been slightly different? “What if there had been a difference of two or three seconds? I could have suffered much deeper injuries, my bones could have broken, or I could have died on the spot,” she said.The Ciaz sped away after the crash. One of Shivani’s friends chased it and caught up with it at a traffic signal, but Shivani said the driver denied responsibility and left again. The accused, Kalyan Bainsla (33), later gave a media interview, claiming a group of bikers had been riding aggressively and that Shivani suddenly turned while he was taking a U-turn. He denied hitting her deliberately.Shivani rejected the version. “If you felt so bad for me, why did you not stop at that time?” she asked, questioning why nobody checked on her after the collision.Police subsequently arrested Bainsla in Rajasthan along with his cousin Lovneesh (32), who was also in the car. DCP (east) Sandeep Kumar said police added Section 109 of BNS, for attempt to murder, after analysing the footage and added that the collision appeared deliberate. Sections 78 and 79, relating to stalking and insulting a woman’s modesty, were also added after Shivani’s statement.For Shivani, the incident is about more than one dangerous ride. “Every woman rider should be able to feel safe on the city’s roads. Unfortunately, that sense of security is still missing,” she said.Sunday was meant to be a simple escape from her routine of helping residents in Kalkaji with civic problems. Her father Roshan Chauhan, an AAP functionary, said she had bought her first motorcycle only five to six months ago. “Her Sunday routine was simple. She wanted to ride out, have tea and return home,” he added.Shivani had gone out with a group of bikers on Sept 13. The family learnt about the crash only the next day, when journalists reached their home.Shivani, a fashion designing graduate, contested the 2022 MCD election on an AAP ticket at 23 and finished second. articles.standfirst: Lançamento da Ascen traz uma leitura contemporânea do luxo, com arquitetura integrada à paisagem e espaços pensados para diferentes momentos da vida
articles.summary: Lançamento da Ascen traz uma leitura contemporânea do luxo, com arquitetura integrada à paisagem e espaços pensados para diferentes momentos da vida
articles.body:
Perspectiva artística da fachada — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação: Ascen

O conceito de luxo residencial está mudando. Se durante muito tempo esteve associado à suntuosidade, pompa e ostentação, agora ganha um novo significado, ligado à qualidade das experiências: ter tempo, encontrar privacidade sem abrir mão da convivência e ambientes capazes de proporcionar conforto e bem-estar.

Perspectiva artística do acesso ao estacionamento — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação: Ascen

Foi a partir dessa visão que a Ascen Empreendimentos desenvolveu o Birdie, seu novo lançamento de alto padrão na Vila do Golfe, na área mais nobre da zona Sul de Ribeirão Preto. Um projeto que oferece o ponto de equilíbrio perfeito entre arquitetura e natureza, movimento e pausa, espaços para recolhimento e também para encontros.

Perspectiva artística do terraço garden — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação: Ascen

Com residências suspensas a partir de 270 m², o Birdie foi concebido para oferecer amplitude e diferentes possibilidades de contemplação da paisagem, incluindo unidades voltadas para o Ipê Golf Club e para a Mata de Santa Teresa.

A relação com o entorno orienta o projeto, desenvolvido pelo escritório internacional Perkins&Will, e que incorpora a paisagem ao cotidiano de quem vive no edifício.

Perspectiva artística da piscina — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação: Ascen

“Buscamos criar um empreendimento que não fosse apenas um lugar para morar, mas um lugar que contribuísse positivamente para o dia a dia das pessoas. O Birdie traz a sensação de que alguém pensou cuidadosamente na experiência humana antes de pensar no produto imobiliário”, define Fernando Vidal, Managing Director da Perkins&Will São Paulo.

O novo luxo: menos ostensivo, mais emocional

A continuidade do que existe ao redor está presente nos interiores do Birdie, assinados por Cacau Ribeiro. Permeabilidade, proporção dos ambientes, iluminação natural, enquadramento da paisagem e presença marcante do verde constroem uma experiência de sofisticação menos associada à ostentação e mais relacionada às sensações despertadas.

Perspectiva artística da suíte master — Foto: - Crédito: Divulgação: Ascen

“Um dos principais diferenciais do Birdie está justamente em questionar a ideia tradicional de que um empreendimento de alto padrão precisa demonstrar luxo através da imponência. Neste projeto, o luxo aparece de outra maneira: na qualidade dos espaços, na luz natural, na materialidade, no conforto e, principalmente, na forma como o morador é recebido”, afirma Cacau Ribeiro.

O paisagismo de Mônica Costa segue o mesmo princípio ao integrar natureza, arquitetura e bem-estar, estabelecendo uma verdadeira simbiose entre a vegetação do empreendimento e o seu entorno.

Perspectiva artística do spa — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação: Ascen

“Isso significa fazer com que o projeto desenvolvido para o Birdie estabeleça uma relação de escala, profundidade e pertencimento com as paisagens externas”, explica Mônica.

A proposta de vivenciar experiências memoráveis se estende às áreas compartilhadas, com a presença de espaços adequados a diferentes momentos da rotina: atividade física, trabalho, relaxamento, lazer, encontros e convivência.

Perspectiva artística do salão de festas — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação: Ascen

Academia, espaço pilates, coworking, espaço jovem, beauty, relax room, saunas úmida e seca, SPA, pool bar, piscina, prainha, espaço família, salão de festas e brinquedoteca estão entre os ambientes previstos. A academia leva a assinatura da Technogym, marca italiana especializada em equipamentos e soluções de wellness.

A localização do Birdie é outro ponto forte. O futuro empreendimento está inserido em uma região marcada pela presença de áreas verdes e pela proximidade com o Shopping Iguatemi e o Ipê Golf Club, no ponto mais nobre da Vila do Golfe.

Fotomontagem — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação: Ascen

Neste cenário, a arquitetura do Birdie se integra em sua totalidade à paisagem natural, permitindo que ela participe da experiência no interior das residências e também nos espaços compartilhados.

Para a Ascen, o Birdie representa também a oportunidade de traduzir em um novo empreendimento a visão de como o alto padrão pode evoluir em Ribeirão Preto: mais atento à experiência proporcionada pela arquitetura, pelas paisagens e pelos espaços de convivência.

“O Birdie é um projeto conectado ao que existe de mais moderno e atual no mundo e ao mesmo tempo muito conectado com o local onde está inserido. É moderno e contemporâneo ao mesmo tempo em que se propõe a ser atemporal”, explica o diretor comercial da Ascen, Ricardo Pagano Junior.

O nome escolhido para o empreendimento reforça a ideia de excelência e superação. No golfe, o birdie é quando o jogador completa um buraco usando uma tacada a menos do que o par (número previsto de tacadas) estabelecido para aquele buraco. Uma expressão associada à concentração e precisão, que vai além das expectativas.

articles.title: ‘She is in a lot of pain, has hidden bruises’: Gurgaon biker’s father; Sia to undergo MRI, X-rays today
articles.summary: GURGAON: The woman biker injured in the Gurgaon Golf Course Road hit-and-run case will undergo X-rays, MRI scans and other treatment at a Delhi hospit.
articles.body: GURGAON: The woman biker injured in the Gurgaon Golf Course Road hit-and-run case will undergo X-rays, MRI scans and other treatment at a Delhi hospital, her father said, as she continued to experience pain from injuries sustained in the collision.Her father said Sia was in considerable pain and that some injuries may become apparent only later.He said she had several hidden bruises following the incident and would visit a hospital in Delhi on Wednesday for X-rays, MRIs and whatever treatment she requires.“After an injury, you often discover later where you have actually been hurt, such as hidden bruises, and she had quite a few of those,” Sia’s father told news agency ANI.Sia also said she was in pain and would undergo further medical tests for some of her injuries. “MLC has been done. For a few injuries, MRI tests and X-ray have to be done,” she told news agency ANI.Sia says she was chased, deliberately hitSia alleged that the accused and others in the car had harassed her before the collision and deliberately rammed into her vehicle.“Whatever happened to me on Sunday morning was recorded on my video. I have told the Magistrate what I faced personally. I was chased, harassed, and intentionally hit; I could have died,” she added.She said she had given her statement before the magistrate and requested the strictest action in the case.Haryana Police have arrested primary accused Kalyan Bainsla from Dausa, Rajasthan, along with co-occupant Lovneesh from Palwal, after they allegedly fled the scene and switched off their phones.Sia and her family have maintained that the collision on Golf Course Road was an intentional attack and not an accident.Her father also described the incident as an attempt to murder and thanked police for arresting the accused.‘Not hit-and-run, but attempt to murder’: Sia’s advocateSia's advocate, Abhishek, said the case was registered under attempted murder provisions based on the manner in which the vehicle hit her and the accused fled the spot."The charges that have been filed are for attempted murder. As is evident from the video, this is not a hit-and-run case; it is an attempt to murder case. Of course, one cannot comment conclusively on the specific intent of the accused at this stage. That is something the investigation will establish. articles.title: Plans to build massive solar farm in Wiltshire edge closer
articles.summary: More than 5,000 people have objected to plans for the 500-megawatt solar farm in North Wiltshire.
articles.body:
The next stage of the planning process for what could be one of the UK's biggest solar farms has begun.

More than 5,000 people have objected to Island Green Power plans to build a 500-megawatt solar farm across 3,000 acres in North Wiltshire and now the final set of public hearings have started as part of a six month examination period.

Anna-Kate Fuller, founder of the campaign group Stop Lime Down, said: "We have worked tirelessly to raise funds from across our community to protect and preserve this part of the countryside."

Will Threlfall, Senior Project Development Manager responded: "We will continue to listen carefully and respond to the points raised throughout the process".

There are several other larger scale sites in the planning process, including one at Botley in Oxfordshire .

Getting a decision on this is a long process, the original application was submitted in September 2025, then the public were invited to have their say.

The plans are now in an examination stage, where any interested or affected parties can share views and evidence about the plans and the examining authority asks questions about the proposals.

The evidence submitted is wide ranging - from the potential impact on individual land owners and businesses, to established wildlife habitats and farming practices on the land in question.

This stage finishes on October 21st, at which point the examining authority have up to three months to make a recommendation about whether or not the scheme should go ahead.

After that, it could be another three months until a decision is made in Spring 2027.

articles.title: Ryder Cup 2027: Team Europe stars give verdict on early trip to Adare Manor and 'fresh energy' for Luke Donald's side
articles.summary: Team Europe enjoyed a practice round at Adare Manor on Monday ahead of the Ryder Cup being hosted there next September; Several members of Luke Donald's side discussed the benefits of the team trip in their BMW PGA Championship press conferences
articles.body:
Although not quite a full scouting mission like Donald provided ahead of previous Ryder Cup wins at Marco Simone GC and Bethpage Black, it gave many of his potential players an early experience of tackling next year's Ryder Cup venue in Ireland.

A mix of established Ryder Cup members and likely rookie contenders made the trip after the Amgen Irish Open, with a team dinner followed by 18 holes on Monday

Sixteen players joined Donald and his vice-captains for the team session ahead of travelling onto the DP World Tour's BMW PGA Championship - 10 of last year's line-up, two more with past Ryder Cup pedigree and four potential debutants.

"Any time I'm asked to go to Adare Manor, I'm going to go happily and willingly," said Jon Rahm. "It's one of the best hotel golf course experiences there is in the world.

"It was a lot of fun. It was very enjoyable. I think those days are great for all of us to see each other and just in a way remember why we do what we do.

"For those players who have never been there before, I think it's just getting those first nerves out of the way of how they may feel.

Only Rory McIlroy and Rasmus Hojgaard were missing from Donald's dozen that celebrated a 15-13 victory in New York. Alex Noren - a winner in 2018 and vice-captain last year - and Nicolai Hojgaard, part of the 2023 team, also made the trip.

Alex Fitzpatrick and Kristoffer Reitan both featured after impressive rookie campaigns on the PGA Tour, while Spanish duo Eugenio Chacarra and Ángel Ayora were the other newcomers involved.

Most travelled straight from the Amgen Irish Open, with Shane Lowry a later arrival after his record-breaking 11-shot win on home soil at Trump International Golf Links.

"It was a lovely boys' day out, in the sense we got together and had a nice dinner," Justin Rose told the Sky Sports podcast . "There was some intention-setting of what it means to be on the team and what the plans are going forward.

"The round itself yesterday was very casual, very fun and just a first look at the golf course. Having Adare Manor pretty much to yourself is a pretty special experience.

"For them [rookies], it lights the fire even more in them to want to be a part of that team. It gives them the comfort to feel like they're already part of the team, in the sense of [being in] Luke's thoughts, the way of doing things and how the captain goes about it.

"It doesn't necessarily feel like a game-changing trip and 'wow, we have an advantage' or anything like that, but I think it's very important in terms of culture setting and all that."

The European players went out in groups of four for a round in calm conditions, with some playing the course for the first time and others refamiliarizing themselves with a venue that previously hosted the JP McManus Pro-Am.

"With the good weather they've had in Europe, in Ireland, it was in as good a shape as I've ever seen it," Rahm added. "It was actually firm. They could have had it as fast as they wanted to.

"It wasn't overly fast because obviously I think they want the public to still enjoy the week. It was in perfect condition. It was immaculate."

The last two Ryder Cups in Europe have been on venues used for regular DP World Tour events, with Le Golf National (2018) a past site of the Open de France and Marco Simone GC (2023) the Open d'Italia, giving Donald a different challenge in Ireland.

"The strategy around setting up the course is very different from when they have a lot of data from the [DP World] Tour," Noren explained. "It's a very difficult task to set that up, I think, to our advantage. We'll see how they do.

"It's the course and the resources where you can set it up pretty much however you want - you can grow in the rough, you can expand, and you can use tee boxes. It's like not particularly a blank sheet of paper, but you can do whatever you want."

Who else was missing and what happens next?

PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai was invited but unable to attend due to a close friend's wedding in Portugal on Sunday, while Tom McKibbin - who played two rounds with Donald in Ireland last week - was not involved.

Ryder Cup qualification is already under way, with points only available via the Race to Dubai standings for the rest of this season before including FedExCup points in January, with Rose expecting to see some new editions in Team Europe next September.

"I think freshening it up a little bit would be a good thing," Rose admitted. "You want your team to be experienced but to have some fresh energy is always great. Whether that be ideas, style of game, pairing options - to change is up is a good thing.

"There's plenty of opportunity for guys to break through. I think the transition from Whistling Straits (2021) into Rome was fantastic and I think that only strengthened into solidifying some of those players that stepped into that role at Bethpage.

There are so many good young players, like the Højgaards [Nicolai and Rasmus], Ludvig [Åberg], even Bob [MacIntyre]. Those guys are now real stalwarts of the team. There has been a great transition in Europe, so we can afford another new batch of youngsters."

Could consistency be key again for Team Europe?

Europe carried 11 of their 12-man line-up and four of the five vice-captains from their 2023 victory to New York in 2025, with the Molinari brothers - Edoardo and Francesco - already confirmed for a third consecutive stint in Donald's backroom team.

Padraig Harrington has been added as a vice-captain on home soil, while McIlroy anticipates the bulk of Donald's last two teams to be back together again in Ireland.

"If there's ever a place to blend rookies, it is in Europe," McIlroy told Sky Sports . "The thing that I preach around the European Ryder Cup team is there's this continuity.

"I think continuity between the captain, the players, the vice captains is a big thing in a team environment. Look, inevitably there might be some new faces on that team, but I don't think there's certainly not going to be wholesale changes.

"I think the nucleus of our team will remain the nucleus. You might have a couple [new] maybe, but I'd say for the most part, as long as everyone plays well and stays injury-free, you're going to have a very similar looking team to what we've had the last couple."

The Ryder Cup will be held from September 17-19 next year, live on Sky Sports . Donald will be looking to be the first captain in history to win three consecutive Ryder Cups.

articles.title: Vikings news: Brian Flores makes eye-opening take on Week 2 Bears showdown
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings defense faces an early-season trial by fire in Week 2, and defensive coordinator Brian Flores is embracing every second of the challeng...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings defense faces an early-season trial by fire in Week 2, and defensive coordinator Brian Flores is embracing every second of the challenge. Following a thrilling 39-22 comeback victory over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, Minnesota now turns its attention to an explosive Chicago Bears offense led by head coach Ben Johnson.

Coming off a historic Week 1 scoring exhibition, Chicago poses a stern test for Minnesota's aggressive, blitz-heavy defensive scheme. Speaking to reporters ahead of the high-stakes NFC North showdown, Flores acknowledged the intricate chess match awaiting his group.

"It's a major challenge, and that's what we all signed up for," Flores said on matching up against Johnson's versatile offense.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Flores noted that going from Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur in Week 1 to Johnson in Week 2 keeps his defensive unit on high alert. Johnson's playbook features an array of heavy run packages, run-pass options, and spread concepts, forcing opposing defenses to adjust constantly on the fly.

Chicago certainly validated Flores' caution by dropping 59 points and 552 total yards in a 59-37 victory over the Carolina Panthers . Quarterback Caleb Williams delivered four total touchdowns, throwing for 269 yards and rushing for 65 yards, while running back D'Andre Swift rushed for 124 yards and three touchdowns. Rookie running back Kyle Monangai added 100 yards on the ground, highlighted by a 61-yard touchdown run. Meanwhile, Flores' unit showed elite adjustments against Green Bay, holding the Packers scoreless over the final 22 minutes while engineering a 29-0 closing run to snatch victory.

Now, Flores must dial up another defensive masterclass at home to slow down Williams and company . Chicago and Minnesota split their intense rivalry series last season, with both contests coming down to nail-biting three-point margins late in the fourth quarter. If Flores can disrupt Johnson's high-powered rhythm on Sunday, the Vikings will secure a pivotal early-season division win and keep their momentum rolling.

articles.title: Tiger Woods: Golfer seen on range for the first time since March's car crash
articles.summary: Tiger Woods says he "can hit pretty much anything" after returning to the range for the first time since a car crash six months ago.
articles.body:
Tiger Woods says he "can hit pretty much anything" after returning to the range for the first time since a car crash six months ago.

The 15-time major champion was seen hitting balls at Liberty National in New Jersey in a video shared on his Instagram , external before the Nexus Cup, a charity event he is hosting to raise funds for his TGR Foundation.

Woods, 50, also held a clinic where he was asked by the master of ceremonies about his game and replied: "I can hit pretty much anything."

It comes six months after the golfer rolled his Land Rover in Florida and had to crawl out of the passenger door of the car. He refused a urine test.

Earlier this month, Woods accepted a five-year suspension of his driving licence and a $1,000 (£742) fine, as part of a plea agreement with prosecutors in Martin County, Florida, after not contesting a reckless driving charge.

It remains unclear whether Woods is preparing for a comeback.

He has not played competitively since 2024 after rupturing an Achilles tendon in March 2025 and having back surgery last October.

After March's road accident - his second arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence - Woods said he was "stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health".

It was the latest in a string of incidents that have littered Woods' recent years.

His marriage ended - as did lucrative sponsorship deals - after he struck a fire hydrant, a tree and several hedges outside his home in a 2009 incident, sparking accusations of extra-marital affairs.

In 2017, he was sentenced to a year's probation after pleading guilty to reckless driving. That came after police officers found Woods slumped at the wheel of his car near his home.

In 2021, Woods survived a serious accident which left him with extensive injuries and he played only a limited schedule since then.

articles.title: DP World Tour: Irish Open moved to July as tour confirms 2027 schedule
articles.summary: The Irish Open will take place in early July next year as the DP World Tour announced its schedule for 2027.
articles.body:
The Irish Open will take place in early July next year as the DP World Tour announced its schedule for 2027.

The tournament, which was won by Shane Lowry at Doonbeg last week, has been moved to 1-4 July because of the Ryder Cup, which is scheduled for 17-19 September.

With the Ryder Cup's slightly earlier date in September, the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth will be played the week following the biennial contest between Europe and United States at Adare Manor in Ireland.

As a result, the French Open will move to 7-9 September.

The Irish Open was previously held in July before moving to September in 2023.

Next year, it will be played at the K Club before the Scottish Open and Open Championship, and will come at a key time in the European Ryder Cup qualifying process, which will conclude at the British Masters on 22 August.

"I'll obviously be there, I'll play," McIlroy told BBC Sport NI when asked about the Irish Open's new date during last week's tournament.

"Field wise, we'll see, I'm not sure. The Scottish Open will be the week after and a lot of guys are probably going to play that.

"But I get it. The Ryder Cup's in Ireland next year and something had to give."

The DP World Tour's 2027 schedule - which features 42 tournaments in 24 countries - will also include three returning events with the Hong Kong Open, the Singapore Open and Open de Portugal.

The season begins this year at the Australian PGA Championship in Sydney on 26-29 November and will conclude with the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai on 11-14 November 2027.

articles.title: 5 takeaways as primaries end, Trump’s final sprint begins
articles.summary: In today’s issue: ▪ Democrats riding high ▪ Fed expected to raise rates ▪ Kennedy Center board votes to close again ▪ Two longshot impeachment attempts The general election season has officially entered the home stretch as the last primaries wrapped up Tuesday and President Trump today is making the first of many promised campaign stops in the coming…
articles.body:
▪ Kennedy Center board votes to close again

The general election season has officially entered the home stretch as the last primaries wrapped up Tuesday and President Trump today is making the first of many promised campaign stops in the coming weeks.

Delaware held its primaries without much fanfare, as no major candidate faced significant opposition. But the elections still marked a symbolic turning point in the election calendar as all states can now shift their attention to November.

And Trump is heading to North Carolina to start as he seeks to boost Republicans in major battlegrounds that are critical to the party’s chances of holding onto control of Congress.

Here’s five takeaways as the election season reaches its final stretch.

The president earlier this month promised to hit the campaign trail for Republicans in 35 races across the country. One stop typically includes a handful of candidates.

First on the list is North Carolina, where former Republican National Committee Chair Michael Whatley is facing a difficult contest for Senate against the state’s popular former governor, Roy Cooper (D).The state is the only battleground that Trump carried in all three of his presidential contests, but his approval ratings remains near record lows.

Trump’s approval has been on the downslope since July, according to the Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) polling tracker . That could make Trump toxic to congressional candidates running in key races this year.

Many vulnerable Republicans have sought to distance themselves from the president in recent weeks, though party leadership is firmly behind Trump’s approach to turn out the base by asking GOP voters to act as if he’s on the ballot .

In North Carolina, the trip comes as Whatley has been consistently trailing Cooper in polls, raising alarms for Republicans trying to keep the Senate, The Hill’s Julia Manchester reports for Insider.

Trump’s falling approval rating is far from the only data that has boosted Democrats’ hopes that a blue wave could be achievable this year.

Democrats have held a steady lead in the generic congressional ballot for months, a margin that currently stands at nearly 7 points on average. A New York Times/Siena poll released Tuesday suggested more good news for Democrats, finding likely voters favor them over Republicans by almost 9 points.

Pollsters also found respondents said they trusted Democrats more on a variety of issues, including healthcare, the economy and immigration.

Democrats have been feeling increasingly hopeful about flipping several key Senate battlegrounds that Trump carried by double digits just two years ago. The most recent surveys have shown James Talarico (D) leading Ken Paxton (R) in Texas, results that led the election handicapper VoteHub to shift its rating of the Lone Star State from “tossup” to “tilt Democrat.”

Polls have also shown former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio) and former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) ahead in their respective Senate races. Republicans got some good news this week, with Cook Political Report shifting the New Hampshire Senate race toward GOP nominee John Sununu .

Republicans’ redistricting wall in doubt

As the Senate battle becomes more competitive, the race for the House majority is only getting more difficult for the GOP. That’s in part because Republicans’ plans to build a safety net through mid-decade redistricting appears likely to yield minimal returns.

DDHQ chief elections analyst Geoffrey Skelley wrote in an analysis Tuesday on Substack that Democrats are forecast to gain an average of two seats across the nine states that redistricted in the past year.

Republicans redrew lines in states like Texas and Florida to oust a few Democratic incumbents, but some of them are favored to hold onto their seats anyhow. And the GOP suffered a blow in the past week as courts blocked a new congressional map in Missouri that would have eliminated a Democratic-held district.

Supreme Court settles mail-in voting question

After months of lingering legal and practical questions surrounding Trump’s mail-in ballot executive order, the Supreme Court’s Monday ruling settled the debate, at least for now.

The decision handed the president another defeat, as the court declined to allow his mail-in restrictions plan to go into effect in time for November’s midterm elections.

Trump’s directive to the U.S. Postal Service would have permitted the agency to only deliver mail-in ballots to those on lists of eligible voters that states would be required to send in to the federal government.

The ruling doesn’t end the legal battle over Trump’s executive order seeking to place restrictions on mail-ins, but it does essentially ensure the move can’t go into effect this year.

Trump slammed the court for its decision , in particular his three appointees whom he said are “not the people I interviewed” to serve on the court.

One other source of political anxiety for the president, in addition to the economic realities, is the spiking cost of gas.

The price of regular gas and diesel have both jumped significantly in recent weeks as the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz continues. Diesel has broken records day after day over the past week at a time of the year when demand and prices usually drop.

The costs are showing no signs of tapering off in the coming days, a trend that couldn’t come at a worse time for the president as the first ballots could be cast. Many states start sending out their mail-in ballots this week.

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Steve Bannon got the headlines as they teamed up in Washington, D.C., to warn about the potential risks from artificial intelligence. As that was happening, first lady Melania Trump traveled to North Carolina and touted the technology for school children. I asked Randi Weingarten , the president of the American Federation of Teachers, if the first lady has a point about needing to integrate AI in schools to stay competitive.

“We have to actually master the technology, but first things first. We can’t have kids addicted to screens,” Weingarten said . “Kids have to learn. They have to learn relationship building. They have to learn how to think,” she added.

For all the talk about regulations, perhaps being lost in the conversation is how AI should be used in schools. In China, AI is taught in elementary schools. One thing I’ll be asking lawmakers is this: does banning AI in schools help or hurt our kids compete globally later in life?

By the way, here’s your chance to ask your questions to Congress. Have something you want answered? Email me at viewersvoice@newsnationnow.com , and I’ll put your questions to Rep. Mark Harris (R-N.C.) tonight in our Viewer’s Voice segment. I’d love to hear from you.

Pennsylvania reported two new measles-related deaths , bringing the total to four this year. Measles cases in the U.S. are at a 35-year high, and there are more measles-related deaths than in any year since 1992.

Three people were killed after a news helicopter for the NBC affiliate in Los Angeles crashed while covering a fatal bus collision Tuesday evening. Those killed were the pilot, a photojournalist on board and a pedestrian on the ground. Two others were taken to the hospital. The crash is under investigation.

The House Oversight and Government Reform Committee voted unanimously to hold Leon Black, the co-founder of Apollo Global Management, in contempt after he failed to appear for a deposition about his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. RATE HIKE LIKELY : The Federal Reserve is expected to lift the benchmark interest rate for the first time in three years today, when the central bank announces its decision at 2 p.m., capping off a two-day meeting.

A rate hike is not guaranteed, since Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh does not provide signals, as past chairs have, about future actions the Fed may take. But at a speech in Jackson Hole, Wyo., two weeks ago, Warsh argued the Fed still had work to do to bring inflation down and stabilize prices, stressing the importance of listening to market signals.

Investors have taken his speech, along with the latest economic indicators, as signs that the Fed will move forward with a quarter-point rate hike, putting the target range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. FedWatch put the chances of a rate hike at 94.5 percent, as of Tuesday afternoon, with a 5.5 percent shot of no change.

The forthcoming decision, less than two months ahead of the midterm elections, would put Warsh at odds with Trump, who backed Warsh for the position with the explicit expectation that he would cut interest rates.

Trump on Sunday reiterated his desire for lower rates, saying, “The United States is so strong we should be paying the lowest interest rate in the world.”

Gas prices and affordability issues have been top of mind for voters, as the war in Iran continues, straining access to global oil supplies.

Meanwhile, inflation has remained stubbornly elevated, at 3.4 percent in August and July and 3.5 percent in June. Before the war, in January and February, inflation was 2.4 percent — much closer to the Fed’s 2 percent target range.

Shortly after the vote, Trump, who is also chair of the board, issued an ultimatum on Truth Social, saying the construction on the building “cannot begin until such time as the D.C. Circuit rules on the Board’s approved name,” referring to the addition of his own name to the performing arts center named for former President John F. Kennedy.

“If the ruling is a negative one, which it should not be, and is not overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court, the Reconstruction and the Renovation of The Kennedy Center will not take place,” Trump wrote.

“The attorneys from the DOJ [Department of Justice] will ask for an expedited appeal, ” he continued. “In the meantime, 17 Million Dollars, raised by President Trump, has been put into The Kennedy Center account to keep it afloat.”

Despite the board’s vote to close the center for renovations, it’s unclear whether the closure will proceed, since a judge issued a preliminary injunction in May barring a previous effort to close the center.

The legislation, named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.), would grant the president the authority to levy tariffs on countries that purchase Russian energy and extend existing sanctions on Iran. Although the measure passed overwhelmingly in the Senate, it has proven contentious in the House, given the new tariff authority it gives to Trump.

The rule vote, which sets up a final vote on a bill, appeared headed for defeat as a few GOP holdouts refused to support it, but Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez provided key support that helped the rule narrowly pass 214-211. This marks the second time this month the two members broke with their party on a rule vote, a highly unusual move that has enraged some colleagues.

Patel testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee as part of regular oversight. Chief among many Democratic members’ concern was whether Patel would interfere in the midterms if Trump asked him to.

“The FBI will follow the law. If there’s a reason to go there because there’s been a violation of law, we will. Otherwise, we won’t,” Patel said in response to a question from Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.).

Sen. Peter Welch (D-Vt.) pressed Patel on Trump’s comments that the only way Democrats could win the midterms is if they cheat. Patel responded that the president has the right to express his opinions, a response that didn’t satisfy Welch and other Democrats.

And in a more colorful exchange, GOP Sen. John Kennedy (La.) grilled Patel over a recent FBI policy change ending longtime bans on selecting new trainees who have engaged in prostitution or bestiality. Read more about that exchange here .

IMPEACHMENT BUZZ : Impeachment has featured heavily in the House’s last week of action before the midterms, with Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) becoming the latest member to introduce articles of impeachment against a member of the Trump administration.

Massie, a frequent Trump critic, on Tuesday introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth , accusing him of “high crimes and misdemeanors” for the war in Iran, the boat strikes in the Caribbean and the alleged free-speech suppression in his targeting of Democrats who called for service members to refuse illegal orders.

Massie has been open in his disdain for Hegseth and the administration’s involvement in foreign wars, and the secretary campaigned for Massie’s primary challenger earlier this year, helping to unseat the libertarian congressman.

Still, the move marked the first time in recent history that a member of Congress has tried to impeach a Cabinet official of his same party.

The same day, House lawmakers voted on Rep. Al Green ’s (D-Texas) effort to impeach the president, accusing Trump of abuse of power for his immigration crackdown that led to several civilian deaths earlier in the year.

The effort failed in a vote of 232-147, with 18 Democrats voting to table the resolution and 47 lawmakers voting “present,” including the top Democratic leaders.

Democrats were taken aback by the impeachment push, since the party has tried to be laser-focused on cost-of-living and affordability issues ahead of the midterms. Democratic leaders issued a statement noting the resolution was brought to the floor without any formal investigation or broader examination into the charges.

“None of that serious work has been done, with the Republican majority focused solely on rubber stamping Donald Trump’s extreme agenda,” the leaders wrote in a joint statement.

But House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) left the door to impeachment open should the Democrats retake the majority after the upcoming midterm elections.

“We haven’t ruled anything in and we haven’t ruled anything out in terms of impeachment,” Jeffries told George Stephanopoulos Sunday on ABC’s “This Week,” when asked whether impeachment of the president would be a day-one priority for House Democrats.

ISLAND ACCUMULATION : The Houthi rebels in Yemen have been gradually gaining more territory by the Red Sea, potentially increasing the chances of another struggle over control of a key waterway.

The rebels recently seized the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish in the southern Red Sea, increasing their leverage around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which is a key alternative shipping lane to the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway goes between the tip of Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula and Djibouti and Eritrea in Africa.

The strait has emerged as even more important of a passageway since Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping at the start of the war. Saudi Arabia has used Bab el-Mandeb for crude oil exports.

But the Iran-backed Houthis’ seizure of the two islands will increase pressure on Saudi Arabia and could give Iran additional leverage in its war with the U.S. The Houthis previously seized the Red Sea port of Mokha and another strategic island.

Trump has taken a notably hands-off approach to attacks from the rebels as they secure a Red Sea chokepoint. The U.S. has sent advisers to support Saudi Arabia, but Trump reportedly refused a Saudi request to launch strikes on the Houthis.

The approach marks a contrast to the early days of the Iran war, when Trump ordered strikes on the Houthis in response to attacks on vessels in the Red Sea launched from Yemen.

Nobody really wants to hear about bright spots after the way the Packers started the season, but there were a few in Week 1, and rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse was one of them.

That's the real takeaway from Cisse's performance. Rising tides in the secondary tend to carry all boats, and every decent performer takes just that much pressure off of everyone else. articles.title: Matt Fitzpatrick: DP World Tour Championship defending champion not comfortable with Dubai location
articles.summary: Matt Fitzpatrick says he is not "100% comfortable" with the prospect of travelling to Dubai for the season-ending DP World Tour Championship in November when he is due to be defending champion.
articles.body:
Matt Fitzpatrick says he is not "100% comfortable" with the prospect of travelling to Dubai for the season-ending DP World Tour Championship in November when he is due to be defending champion.

Fitzpatrick is concerned that the United Arab Emirates could be a target in the ongoing conflict between Iran, the United States and Israel.

"You've only got to look at the hotel that got hit earlier this year," Fitzpatrick told BBC Sport. "I was having dinner the week I won in that hotel.

"That's obviously very scary when you think about how it was a few months away but how close you were to that particular spot and for something like that to happen. It's obviously quite scary."

Fitzpatrick would like to see the event switched to a different host country, a decision he called a "no brainer, in my opinion" before adding: "But I'm not a sponsor, I'm not paying the bills and all that sort of stuff.

"I'm sure there's more to it than just the meets the eye."

Led by chief executive Guy Kinnings, DP World Tour officials are assessing safety issues for their final two play-off events in Abu Dhabi and then Dubai.

Both tournaments are backed by key sponsors of the European-based tour and provide a lucrative end to the season for the circuit's leading money winners.

"I think it's annoying, but at the same time, Guy Kinnings can't control what Iran are doing," Fitzpatrick added.

"It is frustrating because as someone who likes to plan and be prepared, it is difficult to kind of figure out what's going on. Obviously, things as they stand are a bit weird over there.

"I can't say I'm like 100% comfortable, but I guess you just have to see nearer the time and, you know, I still need to qualify as well."

Fitzpatrick's Ryder Cup team-mate Shane Lowry said the tour faces important choices over how to end the current season. "They are huge decisions for everyone," said last week's winner of the Irish Open.

"I'm not going to sit here and comment on the whole thing because I think it's up to the powers above to sort that all out. I think if the tournaments are on, the players are going to go. And if they are not, they will find an alternative."

A spokesperson for the DP World Tour said: "We are in constant dialogue with our members and their management teams about the tournaments they play in, but ultimately players' individual schedule choices are a matter for them to decide.

"As far as our play-offs are concerned, it remains our intention to play as scheduled in the UAE but we continue to monitor the situation and take advice from our international travel advisors."

articles.title: King Charles visits Cairngorms after summer wildfire
articles.summary: Charles travelled to An Lochan Uaine to meet with volunteers and firefighters on Wednesday morning.
articles.body:
King Charles has expressed "admiration and appreciation" for those who helped tackle this summer's wildfire in the Cairngorms.

The king travelled to An Lochan Uaine – commonly known as the Green Lochan -where he met volunteers, firefighters and landowners who were part of the efforts.

The fire broke out in the Glenmore area near Aviemore on July 15 and burned across 3,300 hectares of land for almost five weeks.

In a statement, Charles thanked "all those who have worked so tirelessly and courageously" to bring this year's wildfires under control across the UK.

More stories from the Highlands and Islands

News from the Highlands and Islands on BBC Sounds

He said: "My wife and I have been appalled by the devastating impact of wildfires this summer and the terrible destruction they have caused to homes, livelihoods and landscapes, not only in this beautiful landscape of the Cairngorms, but across the United Kingdom and – as we have seen – other regions of Europe.

"I can only express my admiration and appreciation to all those who have worked so tirelessly and courageously, in the UK and beyond, to bring these fires under control and to those supporting communities facing the long road to restoration and renewal that still lies ahead."

More than 500 firefighters were involved in fighting the blaze, with homes, businesses, campsites and a ski resort in the area evacuated.

Charles arrived in a Land Rover shortly after 11:00 and for part of the visit walked with the assistance of a shepherd's crook as he traversed the uneven ground through woodland above the loch.

Representatives of the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service, the Cairngorms National Park Authority, the RSPB, NatureScot and staff from local estates were among those to meet Charles.

He spoke to them about the blaze, their firefighting efforts, and the damage done to the area.

At one point he could be heard discussing how Caledonian pine trees respond following a fire, and saying it is a "great relief" that the area has now seen some rain.

He also met representatives of other national parks – including the Shenandoah National Park in Virginia, in the United States, which he visited in April.

As part of the visit, Charles marked the new twinning partnership between the Cairngorms and the US park.

The mountains of Scotland and Appalachia in the US formed part of the same ancient range more than 250 million years ago, before geological forces gradually separated them across the Atlantic.

Charles unveiled a piece of granite from Shenandoah National Park to mark the shared geological heritage of the two national parks.

The stone is a companion to the one from the Cairngorms that was unveiled in Shenandoah during Charles's state visit earlier this year.

Cairngorms National Park boss Grant Moir said: "It was great to have him here and to show him the damage that was caused by the wildfire.

"But also to talk about what's going to happen in the future and how we're all working together to ensure these things are minimised in the future, and that we can do more to try and protect these amazing places."

He said the King's visit was "incredibly important" in raising awareness of the wildfire, and of the ongoing work to help the area recover from it.

"I'll give him some support and advice. He hit a good tee shot, which I was annoyed by. I wanted him to hit it out of bounds..."

'Incredible' McIlroy dazzles during Pro-Am

McIlroy, who explained he was "still working on elements of his swing" during his pre-tournament press conference on Tuesday, dazzled during Wednesday's Pro-Am, carding a remarkable 60.

While it was not an official tournament score, it beats his low score of 65 at the BMW PGA Championship, and his lowest-ever score on the DP World Tour, a 62, which he made at the 2025 Abu Dhabi Championship.

Fresh off the back of his tied-41st finish at the Amgen Irish Open, McIlroy was prolific, carding a birdie on the third and an eagle on the fourth hole, before following up with eight consecutive birdies.

"Rory McIlroy was incredible; he was 10-under through 11," Sky Sports Cricket's Broad said.

"He didn't miss any putts, and I was joking with him, saying: 'He's got to wear the same clothes tomorrow, same ball'. If he wants us to walk around with him, he's more than welcome!

articles.title: Packers Film Room: Week 1 blitz of the week
articles.summary: Breakdown of the blitz leading to the Packers first quarter interception in week 1.
articles.body:
Even though the Green Bay Packers ultimately lost their opening game 39-22 in week one, no one has a leg to stand on if they want to blame the Packers defense for this one. Until the last six minutes of the game, the defense stood firm and kept giving the offense chances with the ball. They only surrendered two late touchdowns to the Minnesota Vikings because of field position surrendered by the offense with turnovers.

On the second play of the young season for the defense, they intercepted Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray on an all-out blitz, giving the Packers the ball at their 47-yard line. The pressure forced Murray to hurry his throw, resulting in an errant pass.

The play call was a quarters coverage hot blitz where the defense shows cover-0 from a zone alignment, the standard way to present cover-0 these days.

Instead of playing straight man-to-man, the corners are reading the route distribution of the receivers and a low hole vision dropper will rob anything short over the middle. The safeties are keying on the inside routes of the slot receivers.

The Vikings are in 11 personnel (one running back, one tight end) shotgun empty running a mirrored curl/seam route concept called "HOSS Y-JUKE".

The Packers defensive shell shows man across the board with a zone alignment but they're actually playing quarters coverage principles in the secondary.

The corners are going to play "man on deep" and let anything shallow go underneath. Once they see the receiver sit, they'll bail to the deep quarter to help the safety. The safeties are going to take anything vertical from the inside receivers.

Up front, the pressure brings six and the Vikings have five in to pass block. That leaves one extra free rusher unaccounted for and means Murray has a hot throw. On this throw in the Shanahan/McVay offense, of which Kevin O'Connell is part of, the hot throws are the seam routes and the trips side 6-yard stop route.

Zaire Franklin (No. 44) is mugged up in the A-gap and blitzes as the interior rusher in that gap. The offensive right guard should pick up the blitzing linebacker, making the furthest edge defender the widest rusher, but he lets Franklin go unopposed up the middle.

This shorter time to pressure causes Murray to heave an errant pass up the seam where it hangs on him and is intercepted by Keisean Nixon , who fell off the shallow curl route to sink under the pass.

This was Jonathan Gannon's most effective pressure call of the game and it gave the Packers the ball at midfield, where they were able to drive into scoring range but only for what ended up being a 59-yard field goal.

articles.body:
As the LPGA's Race to the CME Globe wraps up, Annika Sorenstam's name will be taking laps around the Homestead-Miami Speedway.

For the upcoming NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race, Gainbridge driver Michael McDowell and Spire Motorsports have unveiled a special livery for his No. 71 Chevrolet Camero ZL1 that includes an Annika 59 goat, the club's pelican and LPGA logo.

"I'm looking forward to meeting Michael at The ANNIKA at Pelican Golf Club in November and watching the No. 71 Annika Chevrolet hopefully take the checkered flag at the NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race," said Sorenstam in a release. "Thank you to our incredible partners at Gainbridge and Group 1001 for this unique partnership - shining a spotlight and elevating women's sports."

The race will take place Nov. 8, just ahead of The Annika driven by Gainbridge at Pelican, the penultimate event on the LPGA's 2026 schedule.

The car's decklid will also include a list of LPGA players eligible for the season-ending CME Group Tour Championship. On race day, McDowell will wear a caddie-inspired bib and golf pants. The following week, he will take part in the LPGA's Wednesday pro-am as a celebrity caddie. Last year, both Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham played in the event's pro-am.

"I'm definitely not the best golfer in the world, so it's easy for me to appreciate the talented players on the LPGA Tour," McDowell said in a release. "I'm really looking forward to visiting Pelican Golf Club to be part of the festivities and seeing the event in person. I know how important this tournament is to our partners at Group 1001 and Gainbridge, so this is a great opportunity for Spire Motorsports to play an important supporting role."

The top 60 players in the Race to the CME Globe advance to the tour championship and a chance at a $4 million winner's prize.

articles.title: La partida decisiva del futuro del golf mundial se juega en varios tableros
articles.standfirst: El PGA Tour presiona al DP World Tour con las tarjetas para 2028 y éste tiene en su mano la llave para hundir al LIV Golf... O impulsarlo
articles.summary: El PGA Tour presiona al DP World Tour con las tarjetas para 2028 y éste tiene en su mano la llave para hundir al LIV Golf... O impulsarlo
articles.body: El otoño nunca es aburrido en el golf mundial, aunque la persiana bajase para el gran público, en año no de Ryder Cup, con la celebración del último Major, el British que ganó Ryan Fox. Quedan cosas en juego: el Open de España, la Orden de Mérito europea que puede caer por octava vez en manos de Rory Mcilroy e igualar el registro de Colin Montgomerie... Y algo más importante, queda resolver la definición del mapa futuro de este deporte, lleno de alianzas y traiciones. El PGA Tour anunció el miércoles cómo será a partir de 2028 su liga, con esas dos categorías anunciadas, las Championship Series -con los mejores jugadores- y una segunda división, la Challenger Series. Esta tendrá 20 billetes cada temporada para subir a primera, categoría que tendrá, además, descensos. Y desde el Korn Ferry Tour, los 10 primeros también subirán directamente a la división fetén. "Las plazas del DP World Tour dependerán de los acuerdos alcanzados con ese circuito", dijo el comunicado. Esa herramienta de negociación entre ambos circuitos tiene al LIV Golf de fondo también. El PGA Tour ya apretó el futuro del LIV Golf 2.0. alcanzando un acuerdo con el Asian Tour, la liga en la que se apoyaban muchos jugadores de aquel circuito para completar el calendario. Está claro que no habrá 10 plazas para el antiguo European Tour -lo que le convierte a ojos del PGA Tour en el cuarto circuito del mundo- y el número estará estrechamente ligado, cuentan, al comportamiento del DP World Tour con la liga que gobierna Scott O'Neil. En realidad, el DP World Tour tiene gran parte del futuro del LIV Golf 2.0. en sus manos. Con un calendario de sólo 10 eventos, la salida natural para los golfistas para hacer un curso normal -20 ó 22 torneos- pasa por un acuerdo con ese circuito que ya 'amnistió' a cambio de rebajas en las multas a varios de los jugadores del LIV. El problema puede surgir si, como se rumorea, sancionan a los jugadores que abracen el LIV Golf 2.0. Éstos no tendrán donde completar un calendario competitivo y disuadirá a muchos que se lo está pensando. Pero si la decisión es otra -aunque en el European Tour no hay tantas simpatías por el LIV-, entonces ambos circuitos pueden beneficiarse del trasvase de golfistas. Las posturas no deben estar tan cercanas cuando desde el DP World Tour anunciaron el miércoles a bombo y platillo el regreso del Open de Singapur y el del Hong Kong Open, dos enclaves del LIV en la temporada pasada. Mientras, el jueves se producirá una reunión con los jugadores del LIV donde, cuentan, se dará a conocer el proyecto de calendario y algunas informaciones más del nuevo circuito que cuenta con 300 millones de dólares, gracias al apoyo del fondo BC Partners y en un escenario donde los jugadores serán los propietarios mayoritarios (52,5 por ciento). La duda es si podría aparecer España como una de las 10 paradas, aunque no sería Valderrama. Y en cuanto a jugadores. Pues además de DeChambeau, el último en asegurar su permanencia es Thomas Detry, que en una entrevista en 'Today's Golfer' explicó seguir y que había una 'rata' (chivato) en el whatsapp que tienen los jugadores que estaba filtrándolo todo. El belga también reveló que en ese grupo no está Jon Rahm, que se salió el 9 de agosto antes de que concluyera la liga.

articles.title: 2 Vikings That Need to Be More Involved in Week 2
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings found a way to come back and win in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers. It […]
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings found a way to come back and win in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers . It was a great start to the season, but it was far from perfect, and two players on the offense need to be more involved in Week 2.

2 Vikings That Need to Be More Involved in Week 2

It was the Justin Jefferson show on Sunday as he hauled in 92 of the team's 151 receiving yards, 2 touchdowns, and a 2-point conversion. Jefferson is the team's star player and while you expect him to lead the charge you want more from the supporting cast.

The Vikings tight ends did a decent job with TJ Hockenson and Josh Oliver combining for 6 catches, 58 yards, and a touchdown. However, there wasn't a single catch for a WR outside of Jefferson.

It was a quiet afternoon for Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings , who both failed to register a single catch in the season opener.

Addison saw two targets and failed to catch either, though a full-stretch dive got his fingertips on the ball, which was a good effort. Jennings saw just one target which came early in the game when Kyler Murray was still in. Throwing into double coverage, Murray's pass was intercepted in front of Jennings.

Neither Tai Felton nor Myles Price even saw a target.

It was a strange game where the Vikings' offense didn't particularly pull off long drives with the exception of one that was aided by three defensive penalties and finished with an Aaron Jones rushing touchdown. The fourth-quarter dominance of Minnesota 's defense and a long kickoff return from Price set the Vikings up with some excellent field position to help orchestrate their comeback win over the Packers.

Can Wentz Get Into Sync With the Other WRs?

Carson Wentz has shown a good connection with Jefferson dating back to when he played last season. However, the Vikings don't want to rely on it always being Jefferson who makes the big plays.

Up against a dynamic Chicago Bears offense in Week 2, Minnesota will need their own offense to be at its best. With running back Jordan Mason placed on Injured Reserve with a thumb injury this week, that means a lot more Addison, and more Jennings. Three targets between the pair won't cut it.

Addison and Jennings are very different styles of WR, with Addison much smaller, slimmer, and relying on his slick route running and ability to get open on deep routes. Jennings is a bigger, more physical WR who can make plays on contested catches. Minnesota doesn't want the pair drawing another blank in Week 2; Kevin O'Connell would do well to draw up some early touches for both of them, and then it's down to Wentz and the two receivers to deliver.

The Vikings will need everyone firing on all cylinders if they are going to pull off what would be considered an upset win over Chicago.

articles.title: Energy company unveils new slimline pylons designed 'with Welsh landscape in mind' after backlash
articles.summary: Green Gen Cymru says the 22m high single-pole structure was considerably shorter than traditional steel pylons.
articles.body:
An energy firm facing backlash over plans for new power lines has unveiled what it has described as a "slim and compact" pylon, designed "with the Welsh landscape in mind".

Green Gen Cymru said the 22m (72ft) high single-pole structure was considerably shorter than traditional steel pylons, with the aim of "limiting visual impact".

The firm's design has been commissioned for use on two of its three planned routes for upgrading the electricity grid across mid and west Wales.

The Campaign for the Protection of Rural Wales said it was "still a major piece of infrastructure in the countryside".

Green Gen's proposals have previously sparked protests and legal action , as well as a pledge from the Plaid Cymru-led Welsh government to prohibit the use of large-scale steel pylons.

The company said its new pylon had been inspired by "monopole designs commonly used across Europe".

"Monopoles are single-pole structures designed to carry significant electricity network capacity within a slim and compact profile," it explained.

The company had previously proposed using 27m tall steel pylons, whereas this new design would be nearer 22m.

Wooden-pole alternatives are around 12m high but can carry less electricity.

Using monopoles rather than wooden ones would mean fewer overhead lines are needed, the company said, reducing impacts on farmland and scenery.

They have argued that relying solely on putting cables underground is prohibitively expensive and disruptive.

The new monopoles will be used on the firm's Towy Usk and Towy Teifi projects - as part of a "toolkit" which also includes wood poles, underground cables and traditional pylons.

A prototype is expected to be ready to be installed in early 2027 for communities to see.

The firm has issued computer-simulated images of what its new pylons could look like.

BBC News asked passers-by in Carmarthen what they made of the design.

Georgia Rollinson, 27, said she had a pylon outside her bedroom window and thought these looked "a little bit better".

"I think I'd prefer that to one of the others. It might blend in better," she said.

"If people want to live in the modern world with the television and internet then they have to have some sacrifices somewhere - even if it is a pylon in the middle of a field."

Anthony Read, 69, said: "They certainly do look smaller and better but ideally put them underground if you can."

He claimed: "It's all down to cost but if something's hidden it's better for the environment."

Phillip Richardson, 78, asked: "Why spend money replacing [pylons] with something that's only marginally better?

"I can't see them being better for the environment - it's a waste of money and could be better spent."

Robin Daniels, 58, said they looked "a lot better than the traditional ones you see across the landscape".

"We've got to decarbonise and the electricity's got to move somehow," he added.

"Burying the cables is expensive so if this is an alternative to make it a bit less of an eyesore, it's probably a good idea."

Green Gen hopes to build three major powerline routes connecting onshore windfarms planned by its sister company Bute Energy with the wider grid network.

It says it will invest nearly £1bn by 2030, with proposals affecting parts of Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Powys and Shropshire.

But it has faced considerable backlash in certain communities, with groups representing hundreds of landowners recently taking the company to court .

Plaid Cymru also campaigned against pylons ahead of winning May's Senedd election, promising in its manifesto to have "a clear presumption in favour of undergrounding" new power lines.

"Overhead alternatives" would only be allowed "where installation is via low wooden poles or equivalent, less intrusive infrastructure".

Dr Jonathan Dean, from the Campaign for the Protection of Rural Wales, said the new design would not be enough to placate opponents of the firm's plans.

"It is still a major piece of infrastructure in the countryside," he argued, while separate proposals for new transmission lines under consideration by the National Energy System Operator (NESO) could render Green Gen's plans "utterly redundant".

Farmer Dyfan Walters, who lives near one of the company's proposed pylon paths on the outskirts of Llandovery in Carmarthenshire, said "undergrounding is the only option that we would consider and that is very much aligned to the Plaid Cymru policy".

While the new pylons would still be unacceptable to many, he said the fact the company had been forced to change its original plans should be viewed as "a win for the community".

Guto Davies, head of external affairs at Green Gen Cymru, said a range of factors had led the firm to look for an alternative pylon design including "engineering and environmental implications, the community feedback and of course the political landscape in which we're operating".

"We've tried to test ourselves to find an innovative approach" that would help "deliver for Wales' economic, productivity and decarbonisation ambitions whilst also making sure we build around the needs of the communities that are hosting this infrastructure".

Stephen Rowlands, the company's head of construction and supply chain said there was "a real opportunity for Welsh industry to play a leading role" in developing and delivering the new pylons.

"As we take the monopole forward, we want to harness the skills, expertise and manufacturing capability that exists here in Wales," he said.

The Welsh government said it would be "inappropriate to comment on specific planning proposals due to the role of Welsh ministers in the process".

"We are developing a National Energy Strategy so Wales can meet its energy demand sustainably and with more benefit to the people and communities of Wales."

articles.title: Liverpool given green light to sign Andoni Iraola favourite
articles.summary: Liverpool signed four new players this summer. And, while each of them have already had a fairly positive impact on the way that things have gone at Anfield,...
articles.body:
Liverpool signed four new players this summer.

And, while each of them have already had a fairly positive impact on the way that things have gone at Anfield, it still feels like more needs to be done before the Reds are ready to start competing for the Premier League title again.

Indeed, Andoni Iraola's main goal this season will be to try and add some silverware to Liverpool's trophy cabinet but, at the very least, he'll be expected to finish in the top four.

At the moment, the Anfield outfit are unbeaten across all competitions but, the vast majority of their performances have been less than convincing.

So, by the time January comes around, it would be unsurprising to see the Reds try and make a move for one or two more players.

That is, especially since it now feels like Liverpool have been given the green light to sign one of Iraola's former men.

Illia Zabarnyi was entirely left out of Paris Saint-Germain 's squad vs Brest

One of the main defenders to have been linked with a Liverpool move this summer was Illia Zabarnyi .

The Ukrainian hasn't always found himself as a regular feature for Luis Enrique since his move from Bournemouth back in 2025.

Indeed, he did feature in 37 games across all competitions but, in their Champions League-winning run, he only started two of those ties.

Zabarnyi's lack of starts led to the centre-back being linked with an exit from the Parc Des Princes and, now that Enrique has left him out of his squad entirely in their 1-0 win against Brest on Saturday, it certainly feels like an exit could be on the cards again.

The defender can be used as a centre-back or a right-back which, before Ronald Araujo was signed, was one of the main areas that Liverpool needed to upgrade.

And, since Araujo is only on loan to the Reds, it could still become a major problem area for them in the future.

So, Zabarnyi being left out of PSG's squad entirely over the weekend has opened up the idea of the Ukrainian becoming a Liverpool player once again.

And, since the relationship between the Reds and the Parisian's is fairly strong , a deal could certainly be on the cards.

Andoni Iraola could help convince Illia Zabarnyi to join Liverpool

Iraola was the main reason behind Zabarnyi joining Bournemouth back in 2023.

Before the Spaniard asked to sign him, the youngster was playing for Dynamo Kyiv and was signed by them for around £24 million.

At the time, this felt like quite a bold move for a young defender but, he quickly managed to prove that he belonged with his performances being enough to prove to PSG that he was ready for the step up.

The fact that Iraola and Zabarnyi have worked together before could be massive , as, without the Spaniard, Zabarnyi wouldn't have been put on the map as quickly as he was.

And, now that Enrique is leaving him out of his plans entirely, it does feel like another moved could be on the cards for the defender.

His prior experience of the Premier League could also be massive as, with how young and inexperienced the rest of Liverpool's team is, bringing someone who already knows how tough England's top flight is could be crucial.

Obviously, nothing is set in stone yet but, if Liverpool are looking to bolster their defensive ranks in the future, the Ukrainian could definitely be an option that they choose to explore.

articles.title: Starting September 18, new Green Card rules coming into effect: Full list of categories that are subject to the change and those that are not
articles.summary: Tech News News: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) recently announced that starting September 18, it will implement new guidance on the public charge ina.
articles.body: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) recently announced that starting September 18, it will implement new guidance on the public charge inadmissibility determination. The rules expand financial scrutiny for most family and employment-based Green Card applicants, requiring officers to assess whether individuals are likely to rely on government assistance. The updated guidance applies to all adjustment of status applications (Form I‑485) submitted on or after this date. Older versions of the form will no longer be accepted. Under the new rules, USCIS officers will conduct a stricter public charge test. Applicants will be evaluated on age, health, family status, assets, financial resources, education, and skills. Receipt of means‑tested public benefits after September 18 will count against applicants, while past cash assistance and long‑term institutionalization will also be considered.What is changing: USCIS' new policy guidanceThe public charge ground of inadmissibility has long allowed the government to deny a green card or visa if an applicant is judged likely to become dependent on government assistance. What's changing is not the existence of the test itself, but which benefits count as evidence against an applicant, and how heavily they weigh.Under the outgoing 2022 rule, only two things counted: cash assistance for income maintenance, and long-term institutionalisation at government expense. The new guidance broadens this considerably, allowing USCIS officers to weigh a far wider range of means-tested public benefits, including food stamps (SNAP), Medicaid, and housing vouchers, when deciding whether to approve an application.Crucially, USCIS will assess cases based on the filing date, not the decision date:* Filed on or after September 18, 2026: the new, broader 2026 guidance applies.* Filed between December 23, 2022 and September 17, 2026: the narrower 2022 rule continues to apply, even if the case is decided after September 18.* Filed before December 23, 2022: the older 1999 Interim Field Guidance applies.This means two applicants with an identical fact pattern — say, a benefit received by a household member years earlier — could see very different outcomes purely based on which filing window their case falls into.Officers are directed to weigh the "totality of circumstances" rather than apply a single bright-line test, considering five statutory factors: age, health, family status, financial resources and assets, and education and skills. A Form I-864 Affidavit of Support may also be considered where applicable, along with a newly required, updated edition of Form I-485.Categories subject to the new ruleThe revised public charge ground applies to:* Green card applicants in the family-based, employment-based, and diversity visa (lottery) categories, whether adjusting status inside the U.S. or applying for an immigrant visa abroad* Religious worker applicants* Certain individuals applying for admission to the U.S. on specific nonimmigrant visas* Lawful permanent residents who spend more than six months (180 days) abroad, since they are treated as new "applicants for admission" when they seek to re-enter the U.S.* TPS (Temporary Protected Status) holders who later adjust status through a family petition — importantly, holding TPS itself remains exempt, but a subsequent family-based green card application is notCategories exempt from the new ruleCongress has carved out several categories that remain exempt from public charge determinations regardless of the new guidance:* Refugees and asylees applying through those specific categories* Special Immigrant Juveniles (SIJs)* T nonimmigrant visa holders (victims of human trafficking)* U nonimmigrant visa holders (victims of certain crimes)* VAWA self-petitioners (Violence Against Women Act)* Cuban nationals filing under the Cuban Adjustment Act* Current green card holders simply renewing their existing status* Applicants for naturalization (U.S. citizenship)* U.S. citizens, who are never subject to the public charge ground at all* TPS applicants and re-registrants, for TPS itself (though, as noted above, this doesn't carry over if they later pursue a family-based green card)One clarification worth noting: a child's receipt of benefits like Medicaid or SNAP does not automatically count as the parent-applicant's own receipt, unless the applicant is themselves the named beneficiary of that benefit or is separately shown to be relying on it as part of the household's overall financial picture.How determinations will be madeUSCIS officers will weigh five statutory factors: age, health, family status, assets/resources, and education/skills. They may also review affidavits of support and evidence of public benefit usage. Benefits received before September 18 are limited to cash assistance and long-term institutionalization, while after September 18, all means-tested benefits such as food stamps, housing aid, and Medicaid may be considered.Public charge bondsApplicants found inadmissible solely due to public charge concerns may be offered the option of posting a public charge bond, allowing their case to proceed if they can financially guarantee they will not rely on government aid.Get the latest technology news and updates.
